skills.name: Force-extension graphs and uses of elastic materials

note.text:
A force-extension graph for a spring is a straight line through the origin up to the limit of proportionality; then it curves.
• The gradient (force ÷ extension) is the spring constant k.
• From the graph you can read the extension for any load, or the load for any extension.
Uses of elastic materials: spring balances, car and motorbike suspension, mattresses and chairs, catapults, bows, rubber bands, trampolines, shock absorbers.

sections.heading: Reading the graph
sections.text:
Plot load (N) up the side and extension (cm) along the bottom. For a spring obeying Hooke's law you get a straight line through the origin.
The gradient (rise ÷ run) is the spring constant: if {8} N gives {4} cm, k = {2} N/cm.
To find the extension for a load, go across from the load to the line, then down.

sections.heading: Beyond the limit
sections.text:
If you keep adding loads, the line eventually bends: this is the limit of proportionality. Soon after comes the elastic limit; beyond it the spring stays stretched.
A steeper line means a stiffer spring (bigger k): it needs more force to stretch the same amount.

sections.heading: Elastic materials at work
sections.text:
• Spring balances measure force by extension.
• Suspension springs and shock absorbers in cars, motorbikes and bicycles smooth out bumps.
• Mattresses and chairs use springs or foam for comfort.
• Catapults, bows and trampolines store energy when stretched and release it.
• Rubber bands hold things together because they pull back.

key_words.meaning: rise ÷ run of a line; here load ÷ extension = k
where the graph stops being straight
hard to stretch: large spring constant

examples: Line through ({4} cm, {12} N): k = {3} N/cm
k = {5} N/cm, e = {4} cm: weight {20} N, mass {2} kg

mistake.why: The spring constant is the force needed for each unit of extension.

worked_example.problem: The graph shows load against extension for a spring. Use it to find the spring constant.
steps: Pick a point on the line: {6} N gives {6 / k} cm.

cards.idea: The gradient of the load-extension line is the spring constant.
Read values straight from the line.
example: Go across from the load, then down to the extension.

check.prompt: Use the graph: what extension does a load of {k * x} N give (cm)?

misconceptions.explain: {k * x} is the load; read across to the extension.

solution: The line rises {k} N for every {1} cm.

cards.idea: Springs are used where a force must be measured or a shock absorbed.

questions.prompt: Use the graph to find the spring constant (N/cm).

misconceptions.explain: k = load ÷ extension, not extension ÷ load.

solution: Take a point on the line: {4 * k} N at {4} cm.

questions.prompt: Use the graph: what extension does a load of {k * x} N give (cm)?

misconceptions.explain: {k * x} is the load; read across to the extension.

solution: The line rises {k} N for every {1} cm.

pick.q: Which device uses a spring to measure force?
e: A beam balance compares masses without a spring.
pick.y: The extension of the spring shows the force.

pick.q: Why do cars and motorbikes have springs in their suspension?
pick.r: To absorb shocks from bumps in the road
pick.y: The springs stretch and compress, giving a smoother ride.

pick.q: Which of these does NOT use an elastic material for its job?
e: A catapult stores energy in stretched rubber.
pick.y: A wall must stay rigid; it does not use elasticity.

pick.q: On a load-extension graph for a spring, what does a straight line through the origin show?
pick.r: Extension is proportional to load (Hooke's law)
e: A broken spring gives no line.
The load changes along the axis.
A plastic material does not give a straight line through the origin.
pick.y: Straight line through the origin: direct proportion.

pick.q: After a certain load the graph starts to curve. This point is…
e: The origin is where the line starts.
The spring constant is the gradient.
A zero error is a wrong starting reading.
pick.y: Beyond it, extension is no longer proportional to load.

pick.q: Spring A has a steeper load-extension line than spring B. Which is stiffer?
e: B stretches more for the same load.
pick.y: A steeper line means more load for each centimetre: a larger k.

questions.prompt: A spring has constant {k} N/cm. An unknown bunch of plantains stretches it by {e} cm. Find the weight (N) and the mass (kg) of the plantains. Give the mass.

misconceptions.explain: That is the weight in newtons. Divide by g = {10} N/kg for the mass.
